Senses.Explanation: “The command does not run in vain” (令不虛行) says that an issued order or authoritative action takes effect. Zhugan answers with it when asked why his staff leaps to the thirty-third heaven. An Xingfu attaches it to the white staff that strikes morning and evening. Yikui says recognition of his own position makes his command effective; Baichi places “the house expert’s true command” in a verse; Guantaoqi says it after striking the staff; Yi’an repeats it after directing the assembly to look at the place marked by his staff. The grammatical subjects vary between a command, a true command, and Yikui’s command, but each asserts effective execution.

Senses.Explanation: The question asks why a realized predecessor would move on instead of settling at a seemingly satisfactory point, and it is reused in three separate conversations. In an older Huqiu Shaolong encounter preserved by Hanyue Fazang, an unnamed monk asks why the ancients would not stay here; Huqiu replies that he too is like that, and further questions follow. In Yichu Wuyuan's record layman Shen Yixuan raises a fist and asks the same question; Yichu answers that even Chang'an, good as it is, is no place for a long stay. In Jiqi Hongchu's sermon a monk first offers a response about repaying kindness; Jiqi then asks the headword question himself, and when the monk answers 'after thirty years,' Jiqi rejects both thirty and fifty years as staying. These are three question turns with different local speakers and answers, not three transcriptions of one exchange.

Senses.Explanation: Three teachers revisit Lu Heng's question to Nanquan about a goose that cannot leave its bottle. Xueguan Zhiyin retells the official Lu Heng's puzzle, notes that the question is cleverly set but would have broken the bottle and harmed the goose without Nanquan's response, then asks what happens after it is called out. Juyun Chuiwan Guangzhen challenges Nanquan's one-goose answer by asking how all the egg-born creatures in bottles could be released and answers with images of war and a bird escaping a net. Pu'an Yinsu makes a harsher judgment: the goose ultimately cannot get out merely by a clever call, so he presses whether listeners have themselves responded. The old dialogue supplies one inherited question; the three current critiques differ in what release means.

Senses.Explanation: The old buddha's household style: the inherited manner that shows itself in willows and crows, brothel quarter and crossroads — before any drum is struck. Wuzu Fayan opens with the root couplet — wind mild and sun warm, the old buddha's household style; willows green and peaches red, the patriarch's handle — but then takes it back a step: eyes seeing and hands doing are not yet awake, mouth arguing and tongue tipping run further from the way, what comes in by the gate is not the family treasure; Yuanwu Keqin plants it on every person's bare flesh-ball and every place at Vairocana's crown-door: one machine lifted, a thousand and ten thousand machines pass through; Guxue Zhenzhe answers the knowing-one word with the gate of a hundred ills and then spreads it wider — blue water and cinnabar hills are all one's own self, crow cries and magpie chatter are nothing but the old buddha's household style, down to muddled moods, the three poisons, the nine knots and ten bindings, each one shining, each one freed; Yuan'an Liao grades the formulas themselves: monkey cries and fisher songs are the second sentence, wind preaching ten thousand verses the third — but to wait for the hall-drum and moved lips and then say red-dust market, old buddha's style, willow lane and flower street, the patchrobe's livelihood — how much ceremony is that already? Xiangya Xingting sets an old man in the cosmos, head against the five Sumerus, feet on the four seas, sorting through dust-mote scriptures and showing off the old buddha's household style — how many springs and autumns has this person?; Miyin Zhenchuan, after the shout that gathers two banks' mist, says smoke-rafts and wave-skiffs are all the old buddha's household style and willow paths and flower streets are all Vimalakirti's territory — each thing showing itself within a single dust-mote; Shanyi Ruchun at his installation rules that all the claimants dull each other: to say he completes the predecessor's unfinished case betrays the predecessor, to say he displays the old buddha's household style betrays the old buddha, to say he unveils the true eye of gods and humans betrays gods and humans — and then claps once: the sweating warhorse no one knew, only the fame-covering deed gets re-judged; Meixi Fudu at the loyal-and-righteous hall's founding sets Lord Guan's frosty majesty of old beside today's old buddha's household style in layered auspicious radiance — how far apart are past and present? Two colors, one contest.

The sentence does not merely date an old buddha's death. In the bottle case Yanguan Qi'an makes the requested figure present through the monk's ordinary action before answering that the ancient buddha has long gone. Zhenxie Qingliao later gives the line after asking what has already been missed. These later uses preserve the sentence as a verdict when a questioner looks past what has just occurred.

Senses.Explanation: The Recorded Sayings of the Ancient Worthies is the title of a compiled record of earlier masters and their encounters. The title stands on the work’s own volume heading, while later letters, biographies, and textual studies cite it as a book that can be opened, read, purchased, and used as evidence. Mizang Daokai describes an immediate surge on opening it. Hanyue Fazang’s chronology reports that he sought out its volumes and wept over awakening encounters and exchanges between teachers and students. A Complete Five Lamps biography says Yelü Chucai repeatedly brought material learned from it to Sheng’an Cheng. Zen bends no individual word inside this title; its distinctive work is documentary. The collection carries attributed voices into later encounters, where readers cite, test, contest, and reuse them.

Senses.Explanation: From ancient times to the present gathers the passing ages and today into one time span. Dahui brings all past and present teachers into a single thread and asks listeners to find it in daily activity. Tiebi says neither the past nor present delusions should deceive. Tian’an asks what has changed across the ages. Liaotang imagines the traveling monk of every generation standing before the assembly. Dafang’s verse surveys a scenic lookout and says there has been no second such person through all ages. Yanxi asks how many have shaped and reshaped teaching across the whole span. Shiwu’s verse contrasts short-lived worldly gain with a longstanding human difficulty.

Occurrences.Kwic: 因舉體師叔《古曲偈》
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B25/B25n0144.xml). Zutang Ji (Anthology from the Patriarchs’ Hall). Speaker: source narrator. The Patriarchs Hall narrator introduces Master Ruti’s Ancient Tune Verse when the case is raised. Its opening speaks of the ancient tune’s force and a later line says buddhas and patriarchs lose the trail. Zhaoqing is then asked about that later line and answers through a discussion of leaving no seam or trace. The headword in the introduction names the verse; Ruti is its cited author, not the speaker of this introductory clause.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The source narration says 因舉體師叔《古曲偈》 to introduce the cited verse; no direct speaker is named for this introductory clause.

Senses.Explanation: The ancient tune is a Chan image whose sound cannot be reduced to ordinary musical pitch. In a case quoted by Tianyin Yuanxiu, an unnamed questioner asks Fengxue how a tune without notes can be sung together; Fengxue answers with an impossible rooster and straw dog, and Tianyin later debates how that answer should be given. Xiangzhou Yun sets the tune amid a clay ox, wooden horse, singers, and dancers in his own hall address, ending by asking what remains when people meet. In the Patriarchs' Hall, Ruti's verse about the ancient tune is raised in a separate exchange that presses the line about buddhas and patriarchs losing their trail. These are distinct ways to make inherited sound and responsive understanding the point of an encounter.

Huigong Kaixiong, in Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huigongxiong of Baoxianglin, Nanhai, recounts Yingshan Zhiyin questioning Zaishen Hongzan with his own teacher's three prompts. Yingshan asks the cold-spring question and Hongzan answers that the five eyes cannot recognize it. The stored question turn belongs to Yingshan; Huigong is the later appraiser, and Boshan is the source of the set.

Juelang's responses test the act of presenting the question rather than offer another image of water. In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Lianfeng, the biography of the three Lianshan brothers recounts Shilin's visit to Boshan. Wuyi Yuanlai, Boshan, asks the cold-spring question; Shilin answers that dripping water freezes as it drips. Boshan then asks about the unborn grass concealing an elephant and allows him to avoid punishment as a newcomer. The biography's local subject is Shilin, not Lianfeng; Boshan is the speaker of the selected question.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 有主，非具天眼龍睛者，莫能覰見。洞山一日為眾曰：體得佛向上人，方有說話分。僧便問：如何是佛向上人？山曰：非佛。林泉道：為垂一隻手，不惜兩莖眉。保福別云：佛非。林泉道：倒用顛拈子細看。法眼別云：方便呼為佛。林泉道：不惜唇皮，盡情吐露。若也於斯薦得，方信道：有名呼不得，無位可安排。自古至今，無人能識。故靈峰寬遮外羅，出就藏鋒，道：白雲覆青山。雖則體用互興，正偏兼到，其實舌上無十字關，口角有空王印。更須子細參詳，慎勿死在句下。這僧果然究妙失宗，機昧終始，鑽入紅綿套索，跳入碧玉穽坑，道：莫便是和尚為人處也無？靈峰火到頭上，急忙撲撒，道：淥沼徒長蕖。林泉道：休於言下覓，莫向意中求。免致拖泥帶水，那消逐氣尋香？向乾乾淨淨、冷冷清清處，試參頌意。頌曰：雪嶠層層翠鎻深，風生寒岫結重雲。夜來丹鳳冲霄漢，聽曉樵人逐鴈群。師云：氷霜一色，雪片交光。明白轉身，還曾墮位。莫守層層雪嶠，休栖密密霜林。漫貪疊巘堆青，枉戀幽巖鎻翠。非止形興未質，其由名起無名。古聖不安排，至今無處所。直得龍吟霧起，虎嘯風生。轉位回途，從偏入正。功勳不犯，兼帶叶通。雖寒岫暗結重雲，奈春嶺微生皓月。夜來丹鳳，偶爾冲霄。聽曉樵人，虗勞心力。霜鴈既歸塞北，雲流莫背司南。恰如󳬧子過新羅，致使鬅頭空󳾓耳。還知麼？都為此時曾蹉過，故令今日卒難逢。第五十八則廣教冀州第五十八則廣教冀州示眾云：無師智、自然智，沒可思量；分別心、取捨心，決難裁斷。莫有摸索著知下落者麼？舉：僧問蘄州廣教志和尚：是甚麼物？學人不會。志云：生在冀州。師云：有物先天地，無形本寂寥。能為萬象主，不逐四時凋。林泉恁麼舉來，會那不會？若言會，情存一念悟，寧越舊時迷？若言不會，虗生浪死，有甚了期？向端的處道將一句來。黃蘗云：打破大唐國，覓箇不會的不得。又石頭和尚云：衲帔蒙頭萬事休，此時山僧都不會。又慈覺云：釋迦猶不會，迦葉豈能傳？若會得這不會的，甚生次第？六祖大師告眾曰：吾有一物，無頭無尾，無名無字，無背無面，諸人還識否？荷澤出曰：是諸法之本源，乃神會之佛性。祖曰：向汝道無名無字，汝便作本源佛性。澤禮拜而退。祖曰：此子向後設有把茆蓋頭，也只成得箇知解宗徒。林泉道：靈山授記，也不似今日這僧不會。荷澤誇：知畢竟此物是何模樣？不似廣教說得道理好。待道是識，誇空花之濃淡，定兔角之

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 古聖不安排，至今無處所；其死也

Senses.Explanation: The ancient sages did not set it in place; to this day it has no fixed location refuses a ready-made scheme or a spot where the living matter could be stored. Xuansha places the line after images of a person who will not stay in a cage or turn back when called. Miyun gives it to students leaving retreat and says they should not merely follow his own words. Lüyan asks why the river and moon each have a definite place if the line is true. Linquan puts the line into a comment about not lingering on a frozen mountain image. Gulin calls it part of living speech while warning that the same sort of phrase can become dead when handled as a formula.

Senses.Explanation: The bright pearl in a tray is a figurative image for responsive functioning that is already complete, manifest, and unobstructed. Hanxiu makes the image explicit with 縱橫無礙, 'freely in every direction'; Jianguan follows it with 'rolling and lively'; and Baizhao says it turns by itself without being pushed. The phrase does not describe a literal jewel inventory. Its force comes from a round pearl moving freely as the tray shifts, hence responsiveness without external forcing or obstruction.
